findings.problem: The proof ends with a gluing step that two other proofs repeat. Each one applies `exists_measurable_weakGradient_on_time_union` to a single time interval `J`, wrapped as the constant family `fun _ : ℕ => J` with `iUnion_const`, `fun _ => measurableSet_Ioo` and `fun _ => hp`. Each then discards the third conjunct (the uniqueness clause) with `hweak.mono (fun _ hs i => ⟨(hs i).1, (hs i).2.1⟩)`. The same pattern is in `collar_measurable_pressure_gradient_of_sws` and `theoremB_measurable_pressure_gradient_of_sws`. All three also rebuild the same hypotheses: an open ball `B`, `U ⊆ B` with `closure U` compact, `IntegrableOn p (B ×ˢ J)`, and a per-component a.e. slice statement. The ℕ-indexing is awkward bookkeeping that is only needed for the general union lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Add one single-interval lemma next to `exists_measurable_weakGradient_on_time_union` in WeakGradientGluingTMeasurable.lean. Its statement: for `hB : IsOpen B`, `hU : IsOpen U`, `hUc : IsCompact (closure U)`, `hUB : closure U ⊆ B`, `hJ : MeasurableSet J`, `hp : IntegrableOn p (B ×ˢ J) volume`, and `hslice : ∀ k : Fin 3, ∀ᵐ s ∂volume.restrict J, ∃ g, LocallyIntegrableOn g B volume ∧ HasWeakPartialDerivOn B k (fun x => p (x, s)) g`, conclude `∃ Dp, Measurable Dp ∧ ∀ᵐ s ∂volume.restrict J, ∀ k, LocallyIntegrableOn (fun x => Dp (x, s) k) U volume ∧ HasWeakPartialDerivOn U k (fun x => p (x, s)) (fun x => Dp (x, s) k)`. The proof is the existing three-line argument: apply the union lemma with `J := fun _ => J`, `iUnion_const`, `fun _ => hp`, then `.mono` to drop the uniqueness clause. Here the call becomes `exists_measurable_weakGradient_on_interval (isOpen_vec3Ball _ _) (isOpen_vec3Ball _ _) (isCompact_closure_vec3Ball ..) hUB measurableSet_Ioo hp hslice`, and its output is exactly the goal on `J`. The collar and Theorem B proofs then end with the same one-line call. In all three, `hp` and `hslice` keep their current hypotheses.
findings.benefit: This removes the repeated ℕ-family wrapping and the repeated projection of the first two conjuncts from three proofs. A reader sees directly that a measurable gradient is glued from one interval's slices. If the union lemma's conclusion changes, only one adapter needs editing, not three call sites. The gain is modest, because the three call sites are each only a few lines.

have hUB : closure (vec3Ball z₀.1 (R / 2)) ⊆ vec3Ball z₀.1 (3 * R / 4) := by
    rw [closure_vec3Ball (by positivity : 0 < R / 2)]
    intro x hx
    change vec3EuclideanNorm (x - z₀.1) ≤ R / 2 at hx
    change vec3EuclideanNorm (x - z₀.1) < 3 * R / 4
    exact lt_of_le_of_lt hx (by linarith only [hR])
findings.problem: `hUB` re-proves, step for step, the library lemma `closure_vec3Ball_subset_vec3Ball`. The proof is: rewrite with `closure_vec3Ball`, unfold the norm membership, then `lt_of_le_of_lt hx hrs`. That lemma is in SliceSelectedGradientSymmetricGeometry, which this file already imports. The sibling collar and Theorem B proofs call it in one line.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the block with `have hUB : closure (vec3Ball z₀.1 (R / 2)) ⊆ vec3Ball z₀.1 (3 * R / 4) := closure_vec3Ball_subset_vec3Ball (by positivity) (by linarith only [hR])`. The hypotheses `0 < R / 2` and `R / 2 < 3 * R / 4` follow from `hR`, and `positivity` closes the first.
findings.benefit: This drops six lines of unfolding and keeps one proof of the closure-in-ball fact, which the sibling files already use.
